newsitem.title: ITALY: Britain stays tough on more EU integration.
newsitem.headline: Britain stays tough on more EU integration.

text.p: Britain hit out on Tuesday at calls by some of its European Union partners for closer integration, questioning whether the bloc had embarked on what it called another "lurch in a federalist direction".
Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said proposals by the Dutch EU presidency to give the EU more powers to decide immigration and asylum policies were "totally unacceptable".

He also criticised proposals by France and Germany to bring the Western European Union defence group under the EU and said Britain opposed a Dutch suggestion that foreign policy decisions should be taken by majority vote.

"Foreign policy is always the prerogative of the members states acting intergovernmentally," Rifkind told a news briefing during a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Rome to discuss progress on the drive to reform the bloc's treaties.
"The European Union is not a state. It should not aspire to act like a state," Rifkind said.

Britain's Conservative government, facing a general election on May 1 which opinion polls say it will lose, has been the most reluctant of the EU's 15 states to countenance further integration and the accompanying loss of national sovereignty.

Rifkind reserved his deepest criticism for what he said were proposals to make immigration and asylum policy a prerogative of EU institutions, including the bloc's unelected Commission and the European Court of Justice.

He questioned whether treaty reviews, known in EU parlance as inter-governmental conferences, were attempts by some partner states to override past treaties and take the bloc on what he called "a lurch in a federalist direction".
"If that is the plan, then people should say so," Rifkind said.
